ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ has a vertex angle of $120^\circ$ and $AB = AC$, with $EC = 4$. By folding $\triangle ABC$ so that point $B$ coincides with point $A$, with the crease being $DE$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that by folding triangle $ABC$ such that point $B$ coincides with point $A$, the fold line is $DE$,\\
it follows that $BE=AE$, and $\angle B = \angle BAE$,\\
given $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle C = \angle BAE = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-120^\circ)=30^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle EAC = 120^\circ - 30^\circ = 90^\circ$,\\
in right triangle $AEC$, $AE = \frac{1}{2}EC = 2$;\\
in right triangle $AED$, $DE = \frac{1}{2}AE = \boxed{1}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ has a vertex angle of $120^\circ$ and $AB = AC$, with $EC = 4$. By folding $\triangle ABC$ so that point $B$ coincides with point $A$, with the crease being $DE$, what is the length of $DE$?
raw_record.answer: Given that by folding triangle $ABC$ such that point $B$ coincides with point $A$, the fold line is $DE$, it follows that $BE=AE$, and $\angle B = \angle BAE$. Given $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=120^\circ$, it follows that $\angle B = \angle C = \angle BAE = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-120^\circ)=30^\circ$. Therefore, $\angle EAC = 120^\circ - 30^\circ = 90^\circ$. In right triangle $AEC$, $AE = \frac{1}{2}EC = 2$; in right triangle $AED$, $DE = \frac{1}{2}AE = \boxed{1}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is the upper vertex, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the horizontal base; E is located on BC and close to B; D is located on AB; segment DE is the crease, and the figure also uses a dashed line to indicate the part from B to D, matching the illustration of folding B onto A. Reasoning: Because the folding makes B coincide with A, the crease DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, so E lies on the crease and satisfies EA = EB, and D is the foot of the perpendicular on AB. Given AB = AC and vertex angle ∠BAC = 120°, the two base angles of isosceles triangle ABC are ∠B = ∠C = (180° - 120°)/2 = 30°. Since E is on BC, ∠ABE = 30°; also EA = EB, so in triangle ABE, ∠BAE = ∠ABE = 30°. Thus ∠EAC = ∠BAC - ∠BAE = 120° - 30° = 90°. In right triangle AEC, ∠C = 30°, and EC = 4 is the hypotenuse, so the side opposite 30°, AE = EC/2 = 2. Next look at right triangle AED, DE ⟂ AB, and ∠DAE = ∠BAE = 30°, AE = 2 is the hypotenuse, so DE = AE/2 = 1.
